summary: Generated interfaces can trade development speed for inconsistency, security exposure, cache complexity, and user disorientation.

points.text: Frequent layout changes impair spatial learning and make instructions, support material, and screenshots unreliable, especially for keyboard and assistive-technology users.
An allowlisted component can still be assembled into a deceptive or unsafe workflow, such as hiding consequences, reversing button hierarchy, or binding an action to the wrong resource.
Generation latency, model cost, and nondeterminism complicate debugging and incident reproduction. Caching reduces runtime cost but increases invalidation and rollback burden.
For stable high-traffic workflows, a designed and tested UI may be cheaper over its lifetime and deliver better accessibility, localization, analytics, and performance.
